decisions.rationale: Names the specific hereditary condition of fifth complement component deficiency (C5 deficiency) in the title; a single defined disease, not a general class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: C5-deficient is a disease-derived adjective modifying the noun serum (C5-deficient human serum), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: Second occurrence of hereditary C5 deficiency as the disease name in the abstract; duplicate mentions must each be annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: C5 here denotes the complement protein component itself, not a disease name.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (only disease mentions are annotated)

decisions.rationale: C5-deficient again modifies serum (C5-deficient human serum), used as a Modifier rather than a standalone disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: Abbreviation C5D stands for C5-deficient and modifies serum (C5D human serum), so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers); What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions)

decisions.rationale: C5D modifies the noun serum (C5D serum), functioning as a Modifier for another concept.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: Systemic lupus erythematosus is a named specific disease from which the proband suffers.
C5 refers to the complement component the proband lacks, a protein rather than a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (only disease mentions are annotated)

decisions.rationale: Escherichia coli is an organism name used as a source of endotoxin; the disease it causes is not discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism names not annotated unless the disease is discussed)

decisions.rationale: Refers to the C5 deficiency condition in heterozygous family members, a specific disease state analogous to the C7 deficiency example.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); Examples 6 (C7 deficiency)

decisions.rationale: C5D modifies serum (C5D serum) in the opsonization sentence, used as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is an organism (bakers yeast) used as an opsonization target; no disease is discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism names not annotated unless the disease is discussed)

decisions.rationale: Candida albicans is an organism used as an experimental target; no disease caused by it is discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism names not annotated unless the disease is discussed)

decisions.rationale: C5D modifies serum (C5D serum) in the phagocytosis sentence, used as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: Staphylococcus aureus is an organism used in killing assays; the disease it causes is not the focus.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism names not annotated unless the disease is discussed)

decisions.rationale: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is a named specific disease of the erythrocyte patient used in lysis tests.
Salmonella typhi is an organism used in bactericidal assays; the disease typhoid is not named or discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism names not annotated unless the disease is discussed)

decisions.rationale: Abbreviated form of the organism Salmonella typhi used in lysis experiments; no disease is discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism names not annotated unless the disease is discussed)
